meta.note: Each area joins the capital-cost schedule to the imagery and to what the place earns. Loaded cost applies the limb's own prelims, fees and contingency to that area's net. The images are indicative and nothing here is designed or consented.

top_lines.desc: Guestroom fit-out, first and second floors
MEP adaptation for hotel use - power, data, public health, controls, BMS
Main production kitchen - relocation and extension
Guestroom FF&E, 17 keys
Public areas - restaurant, bar, lounge, reception, private dining
Back of house - housekeeping, stores, staff facility, goods-in, laundry

areas.what: The Grade I house. Seventeen of the sixty keys, the destination dining room, the bar and the afternoon-tea room, and the rooms an exclusive-use buyout is bought for.
areas.works: A soft and FF&E strip-out throughout, structural alteration for the key plan, a second service lift, envelope and roof repair, and comfort cooling retrofitted through listed fabric on the first and second floors, which the ground floor already has.
areas.earns: Seventeen keys, the Main House restaurant at one sitting of 49 covers, the bar, and afternoon tea. The house is also what the fifteen exclusive-use buyouts are sold on.
areas.watch: The measured survey does not exist. The Main House area basis varies from 1,815 m² to 4,162 m² across four documents in the data room.

top_lines.desc: New-build courtyard ranges - substructure, frame, envelope, roof

New-build courtyard ranges - mechanical, electrical, public health, comfort cooling
New build within and above retained walls - structure and envelope
New build within and above retained walls - guestroom fit-out
Conversion of retained fabric to keys - structure and envelope

areas.what: The stables and courtyard ranges. Forty-three of the sixty keys, the arrival court and the all-day room.
areas.works: Conversion of the ranges to guest accommodation at a composite rate, new-build infill where the plan requires it, and the courtyard surfaces, services and arrival sequence.
areas.earns: Forty-three keys — the larger part of the rooms business, and the reason the scheme reaches sixty without touching the principal rooms of the house.
areas.watch: The consented courtyard bedroom count is fifteen, not forty-three. 23/07590/LBC consents offices, staff accommodation and storage in these ranges.

areas.label: The Riding School

top_lines.desc: MEP - restaurant services, heating and cooling, kitchen services, life safety
Event volume and all-day dining fit-out - demountable, ground floor
Roof structure - replace 2 trusses and 30% of rafters, purlins and ridge boards; ply sarking
Demountable furniture, event and dining FF&E
Fenestration - reinstate Wyatt lunettes and Diocletian windows, brick infills, south doors
Structural reinforcement following removal of stabilising cross walls

areas.what: The Riding House. The estate's only large covered volume, restored as a single two-storey space.
areas.works: A restored volume with services rather than a fitted restaurant: the inserted floor stays out, which is both the consented position and the cheaper one.
areas.earns: The events business — fifteen exclusive-use buyouts and fifteen corporate events a year — and the courtyards' all-day room. It is the room that makes the food and beverage margin defensible.
areas.watch: The consented scheme removes the mezzanine to restore the single volume, endorsed by Historic England. Building it back would cut against the consent as well as the cost.

top_lines.desc: New spa building - substructure, frame, envelope, roof and pool tank
New spa building - fit-out: treatment rooms, thermal suite, changing and gym
Spa FF&E, treatment equipment and thermal experiences
New spa building - MEP, pool water treatment, air handling and thermal plant
Concert Hall - restoration of fabric, roof, envelope and structure, dry use
Concert Hall - fit-out: relaxation hall, movement studio, reception and retail

areas.what: The wellness programme: about 2,000 m² across a new building beside the Concert Hall, the church itself as a dry room, and the garden.
areas.works: A new pool hall, thermal suite and treatment rooms built beside the listed church rather than inside it, with the church restored as a dry room — relaxation, movement studio and reception — and an outdoor garden with vitality pool, cold plunge and sauna.
areas.earns: Twelve treatment rooms and the day-pass programme. With the courts and the garden it is also the whole physical case for a capped membership.
areas.watch: No application exists for anything on this site, and the Concert Hall is the Grade II listed Church of St Anne. Both Six Senses and Rocco Forte put the spa inside it.

top_lines.desc: River wall and bank erosion works
River Club building - raised deck above flood level, frame, envelope and roof

Regatta marquee - permanent base, slab, anchors, services for 200-500 pax
Long Water bank strengthening

areas.what: The Thames frontage: a permanent River Club building, the landing stages, and the Long Water isolated and treated for swimming.
areas.works: A 400 m² building raised above flood level with its own kitchen and fit-out, landing stages and boathouse repair, bank protection, and the sluice and treatment that make the Long Water swimmable.
areas.earns: Its own food and beverage outlet at riverside prices, and the Regatta programme. Switching the whole limb off costs about a point of return.
areas.watch: The Long Water cannot be swum unless it is isolated. Thames water at this reach failed bathing standards in almost half of 27 tests before the last Regatta.

top_lines.desc: Residences shell and structure - 12 units x 5,500 sqft
Residences fit-out - furnished to hotel standard
Residences curtilage externals - gardens, drives, boundaries within plots
Community Infrastructure Levy - residences (Class C3)
Plot service connections - power, water, foul, telecoms (12 plots)
Residential estate road and private drive to 12 plots

areas.what: Twelve houses on the Savills-advised plots, sold rather than operated.
areas.works: Estate road and services to twelve plots, the houses themselves, the landscape framework and the statutory provision. The figures on this page are the itemised residential lines alone. The limb also carries a share of the estate infrastructure the houses use, which is why chapter 05 shows the residential budget at £44.97m and £3.75m a unit against the £37.01m and £3.08m here.
areas.earns: Sale proceeds across a single tranche at an absorption of 3.75 a year, not rental income. Both Six Senses and Rocco Forte assume a branded rental pool instead.
areas.watch: No residential application has ever been made on this estate. Planning is at pre-application, and twelve units sits above the affordable-housing threshold.
